title: Hosted API Tool Synthesis & Sculpting PRD (draft)
content:
Context and quick summary:
This doc is an exploratory PRD sketch for a lightweight, latency-first approach to composing streaming generation + tool-calling + structured output that maps neatly to SDK ergonomics so product teams can ship end-to-end features with predictable behavior. The working name is 'Tool Synthesis & Sculpting' — focused on shaping model output into actionable tool invocations while keeping the hosted streaming primitive compact and debuggable.

Problem we want to solve (root cause):
- Users building real-time assistant features struggle with brittle toolcall parsing and high surface area in SDKs.
- Longwave streaming + mid-stream tool calls create state reconciliation problems for clients (partial JSON, multi-frame tool args).
- Existing heavy-handshake protocols add latency; simpler apps prefer predictable, small frames and clear fallback behavior.

Goals (success criteria):
- Define a minimal streaming frame set that supports progressive text + discrete tool call frames + structured checkpoints.
- SDKs expose a simple developer surface: onToken/onToolCall/onStructuredChunk with clear defaults and opt-in advanced hooks.
- Reduce client/server handshake RTT for typical mobile/web use-cases < 20ms added overhead from tooling layer.
- Provide deterministic reconciliation rules so offline replay and resumable sessions work.
- Instrumentation: token-level origin (model|cache|tool) and tool-call latency bubbles surfaced in Console.

Non-goals:
- A fully generalized choreography DSL for multi-step tool graphs (out of scope for MVP).
- Heavy server-side orchestration of multi-tool sagas — we prefer declarative tool frames that clients can compose.

Design sketch (protocol primitives):
- FRAME types (compact names):
  - TEXT: incremental text chunk (string).
  - TOOL_INTENT: a lightweight suggestion block (name + minimal args-in-progress) that signals model intent to call a tool later; optional, can be suppressed.
  - TOOL_CALL: an authoritative tool invocation frame with id, name, args (structured), and optional partial flag.
  - STRUCT_CHK: structured checkpoint (JSON-ish envelope) that indicates a semantic boundary (e.g., final response object or intermediate summary).
  - META: telemetry/diagnostic frames (origin markers, confidence, model-version).

Notes on TOOL_CALL frames:
- Primary constraint: TOOL_CALL.args must be an opaque string by default to keep protocol minimal; SDKs offer parsed helpers and validators.
- For large tool payloads (attachments), TOOL_CALL can include a reference URL or attachment id and a small inline summary.
- TOOL_CALL supports "preflight" status: PREPARE -> ACK -> RESULT. We only implement PREPARE/ACK in advanced mode; default is fire-and-forget with result later as TOOL_RESULT frame.

Streaming semantics and race conditions (client concerns):
- Ordering: frames are strictly ordered. Clients should apply frames in-stream order; TOOL_RESULT frames are matched by invocation id.
- Partial structured output: STRUCT_CHK frames must include a sequence id and final flag to allow client to reconcile partial JSON merges deterministically.
- Resume: sessions expose last-applied-frame-id; client can request resume from last frame id. Server must supply canonical minimal replay to rehydrate cache.

SDK ergonomics (developer surface):
- JS SDK (example):
  - onToken(chunk) => default append to transcript
  - onToolCall({id, name, args, partial}) => returns {action: 'invoke' | 'buffer' | 'drop', metadata?: {...}}
  - onToolResult({id, output}) => returns {apply: true|false} to support local simulation or test harnessing
  - onStructured({obj, seq, final}) => helpful for UI to render progressive cards

- Opinionated defaults:
  - Default onToolCall behavior: attempt client-side JSON-parse of args; if parse fails, emit event with raw string and log telemetry.
  - Retry/fallback: SDK will auto-fallback to a higher-tolerance parsing path (e.g., relaxed JSON, single top-level value) if parsing fails and a developer flag is set.

Structured output guidelines for models:
- We push model teams to emit short, robust structures: {"response": string, "actions": [{"name":..., "args": {...}}], "summary": string?}
- Avoid deeply nested, lossy structures in streaming mode. Prefer small checkpoints (STRUCT_CHK) every 200-400 tokens for long outputs.

Observability requirements:
- Token origin tagging (model | cache | tool) attached to frames; Console shows time-series of tool latency per invocation id.
- Tracing: tie frame ids to request traces and to user-visible session ids.
- Alerts: regressions when tool-call failure rate > X% or parsing fallback engaged for > Y% of sessions.

Compatibility and fallbacks across hosted/dedicated/private modes:
- Protocol is intentionally thin; hosted will provide advanced hooks (PREPARE/ACK) behind feature flag for Dedicated and Private customers who want guaranteed tool guarantee semantics.
- Private deployments may opt to disable telemetry frames (META).

Security considerations:
- TOOL_CALL.args default to text; SDK must not auto-execute tool invocations — it must surface developer callback and require explicit mapping to internal APIs.
- Attachments referenced by id must use pre-signed, short-lived URLs.

API examples (pseudo):
- server stream frames (simplified):
  TEXT: "OK, here's the plan..."
  TOOL_INTENT: {name: 'calendar.create', hint: 'create meeting tomorrow 10am'}
  TOOL_CALL: {id: 't-123', name: 'calendar.create', args: '{title: "Sync", start:...}'}
  TOOL_RESULT: {id: 't-123', output: 'created: meeting_id=abc'}
  STRUCT_CHK: {seq: 42, final: true, obj: '{"response":"Meeting created","actions":[] }'}

Rollout plan (minimum viable):
- Phase 0 (research): implement SDK hooks in JS + mobile shim, simulate protocol over current streaming infra (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (alpha): enable minimal FRAME set (TEXT, TOOL_CALL, TOOL_RESULT, STRUCT_CHK, META) behind feature flag; targeted partners (4 weeks).
- Phase 2 (beta): add TOOL_INTENT + PREPARE/ACK quick path; SDK ergonomics polish and Console telemetry UI (6 weeks).

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in next sync):
- How do we charge for toolcall-attached attachments vs token accounting? (finance input required)
- Should we make TOOL_CALL.args formally typed (schema) at protocol level or let SDKs enforce mapping?
- Backpressure model: do we expose an explicit backpressure frame or rely on connection-level TCP flow control?

Immediate next actions (todo):
- Spike: build minimal JS SDK shim that translates between existing streaming frames and the proposed minimal set (Elliot).
- Write compatibility test harness for resumable sessions (Priya).
- Draft Console mockups for per-tool latency and failure breakdown (Marco).

Quick notes to self:
- Keep protocol intentionally conservative; prefer client-side opt-in complexity rather than server imposing heavy semantics.
- Document explicit deterministic merge rules for STRUCT_CHK (how to merge arrays/objects) — high priority for replay correctness.

End of sketch. This is an early working doc — expect rough edges. Use it to guide a short spike and a partner alpha.
